title: Declare SLI contract: request-level quality and latency plus error-budget reconciliation
creator: Diego Martinez
description: Create a formal, machine-readable SLI contract for request-level quality and latency for per-endpoint/per-model obligations. Define measurement windows, aggregation, error-budget reconciliation process, multi-region failover triggers, and concrete circuit-breaker + load-shedding thresholds. Deliverables: SLI spec doc, dashboards, automated alerts, and a tested failover runbook.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Specified SLIs for RequestAvailability, RequestLatency (p50/p95/p99), and SemanticQuality with precise query-level predicates and aggregation logic
A2: Error budget reconciliation runbook (weekly cadence) that describes signals, owners, and mitigation playbook
A3: Dashboards created for each endpoint/model that show burn rate, remaining budget, and latency quantiles over 1h/6h/30d windows
A4: Automated PagerDuty alert when any endpoint's 30m burn rate > 2x baseline or remaining budget < 20%
A5: Failover policy implemented: automated regional failover policy in soft-mode (no traffic shift) and validated in staging via canary test
A6: Circuit breaker + load-shedding rules deployed to runtime config with integration tests that simulate regional capacity loss and high error-budget burn
sli_definitions: RequestAvailability: fraction of requests that return HTTP 200 with valid model response payload (no model-internal errors) over sliding 30d window, measured at ingress gateway with sampling=100%

RequestLatency: p50/p95/p99 of request-to-first-token (TTFT) and request-to-last-token (TTLT) for each route and model variant, measured at the gateway and normalized to per-route sequence-length buckets: <64, 64-256, >256

SemanticQuality: automated pass-rate of golden prompt checks and LLM-eval metrics per release (ROUGE-like similarity + rule-based assertions) measured daily and reconciled to production sample set; fallback to manual review if automated metrics drop >8 percentage points in 24h

CompositeEndpointSLI: weighted combination: 60% SemanticQuality, 30% RequestAvailability, 10% RequestLatency (p95 normalized) for business-critical routes; weights configurable per-route in the SLO manifest
slo_targets_and_windows: Business-critical routes: 99.9% availability, p95 TTFT < 250ms for short sequences (<64), SemanticQuality >= 92% over 30d rolling window
Standard routes: 99.5% availability, p95 TTFT < 400ms, SemanticQuality >= 88% over 30d rolling window
Background/analytics routes: 99% availability, p95 TTFT < 1s, SemanticQuality >= 80% over 30d rolling window
All SLOs must be expressed in the runtime SLO manifest format and support per-region overrides
error_budget_policy: Definition: Error budget = 1 - SLO_target over the measurement window (default 30d). Remaining budget tracked at endpoint+model variant level
Burn signals: 5xx rates, model-internal errors, semantic-quality violations, sustained latency regressions (p95 > target) aggregated into a single burn-rate metric
Reconciliation cadence: Weekly steward review + daily automated summary emails; emergency review triggered when remaining budget < 20% or 30m burn rate > 2x expected

Mitigations: first escalate to on-call, then apply model-variant weight reduction, enable aggressive caching prefix for repeated prompts, switch to a lower-latency quantized variant if quality delta < 4 points
failover_and_cb_triggers: Soft-failover trigger: sustained regional error-budget burn > 40% for 30 minutes AND cluster health < 70% -> notify PM/SE and enable canary failover for 5% traffic to alternate region
Hard-failover trigger: sustained burn > 60% for 15 minutes OR regional capacity < 50% -> automated regional failover of affected routes with traffic split ramp to 100% per policy
Circuit breaker (route-level): open when 5xx ratio > 3% AND p95 latency > 2x target for 5 minutes; cooldown 10 minutes with exponential backoff for retries
Quality-protecting CB: do NOT open circuit for semantic-quality failures alone; instead trigger model-variant fallback to validated lower-latency variant unless quality drops > 10 points
Tier-aware shedding: when CB opens, start shedding non-critical routes first, then degrade model variants in order (full-precision -> 8-bit quantized -> micro-batched condensed models)
Cache-first rule: if prefix cache hit-rate > 5% and CB active, preferentially serve cache to reduce load; ensure cache TTLs and staleness bounds are respected
load_shedding_hierarchy: Priority 0: Safety and compliance routes (billing, auth, audit) - never shed unless region fully unreachable
Priority 1: Business-critical customer-facing routes - degradation only by model-variant downgrades
Priority 2: Low-latency convenience features (autocomplete, inline suggestions) - subject to shedding when burn rate high
Priority 3: Background jobs and non-interactive embeddings/analytics - preemptively shed or queue
Eviction strategy: mark requests with 'shed=true' header; client SDKs should gracefully handle 429 with 'retry-after' and optional cached token response
observability_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-endpoint/model view including burn-rate, remaining budget, quantiles, quality score trend, and circuit-breaker state
Alerts: PD critical when remaining budget < 10% OR composite burn rate > 3x baseline for 15m; PD high for remaining budget <20%
Tracing: sample 100% of error requests and 1% of successful requests for root-cause analysis; attach model logs and KV cache hit metadata
SLO manifest lint: CI gate that fails if new route declared without SLI definitions or without an owner
implementation_notes: We will represent the SLI contract as a YAML manifest (runtime-slo.yaml) that the SLO controller reads. Fields: route_id, model_variant_id, weightings, thresholds, per-region overrides, owners
Start by onboarding 3 pilot routes: chat-bot-critical (business-critical), embeddings-ingest (background), search-assist (standard). Create dashboards and alerts for them first
Integrate with cost telemetry to compute burn-per-dollar metric to inform traffic routing decisions under load
Plan a staged roll: doc + review -> infra changes (SLO controller) -> dashboards/alerts -> staging failover test -> production rollout with canary
